 Judgment

MFA No.101756/2019 is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 29.12.2018 passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gangavathi, in M.V.C. No.322/2016 for seeking enhancement of compensation whereas MFA No.100951/2019 is filed by the insurance company challenging the liability which is fixed on it.
2. The occurrence of accident, injuries sustained by the claimant, coverage of insurance are not in dispute.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the respondents.
4. In the present case the driver of the TATA ACE vehicle No.KA-34/6620 did not have driving license to drive the said class of vehicle.
It is a specific contention taken by the insurance company that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having driving license.
Also as driver of the said vehicle, charge sheet is filed against him NC: 2023:KHC-D:12385 under Section 3 of the M.V. Act and which proves that the driver was not holding driving license.
Therefore, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation by indemnifying the owner.

5. However, as per Sub-section (2) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicles Act, when the Insurance Company established the fact that driver was not holding driving licence, then as per Sub-sections (1), (5), (7) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicle Act, the Insurance Company as if the judgment debtor shall satisfy the claim in respect of third parties at the first instance and then recover the same from owner of the offending TATA ACE vehicle bearing registration No.KA-34/6620.

Accordingly, order of pay and recovery is made as per the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Pappu and Others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another1; National Insurance Company Limited vs. (2018) 3 SCC 208 NC: 2023:KHC-D:12385 Swaran Singh and Others 2 and also as per the full bench decision of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited vs.
Yellavva and Another3.

To this extent, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
6. In the present case, from the medical evidence on record it is proved that the claimant had suffered fracture of fibula and multiple, distal end of the fibula and multiple and other injuries.

7. The tribunal awarded the compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads. Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Loss of future income 1,05,300 K.Palniyamma W/O Manikyam vs Kasimali S/O Hussainpeera on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121167142/
4  2. Pain and suffering 10,000  3. Loss of amenities in life 10,000  5. Diet, Nourishment, attendants 10,000  (2004) 3 SCC 297  2020 ACJ 2560  NC: 2023:KHC-D:12385  charges and conveyance.
 6.
Medical reimbursement.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, a compensation of Rs.40,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering.
Further, a compensation of Rs.25,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
9. The doctor has stated that the claimant had suffered disability at 60% to the particular part and 30% towards the whole body and the tribunal has taken only 15% disability towards the whole body.
Even though the doctor is not a treated doctor, but as a qualified medical practitioner he can assess the percentage of disability.
The claimant has suffered fracture of tibia and fibula bone and was working as helper in the hospital certainly this fracture affects his earning capacity.
Therefore, it is just and proper to take 18% as functional disability towards whole body.
The accident is caused in the year 2015.

Therefore, notional income of Rs.8,000/- per month is taken into consideration,
which is recognized by the NC: 2023:KHC-D:12385 Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
The claimant was aged 50 years at the time of accident.
Therefore appropriate applicable multiplier is 13.

Hence, loss of future income due to disability is hereby reassessed and quantified as Rs.2,24,640/-
(Rs.8,000 x 18% x 12 x 13).
10.
The compensation awarded towards medical expenses and hospital charges of Rs.39,834/- is as per the actual bills and receipts produced.
Therefore, the same is kept intact.

Further, a compensation of Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards incidental expenses like food, nourishment,
traveling, attendant charges, etc.,.

Thus, the claimant is entitled for total compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads. Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Towards injuries, pain and 40,000  suffering.
 2. Towards medical expenses.
39,834  3. Towards loss of amenities.

25,000  4. Towards incidental charges like 15,000 K.Palniyamma W/O Manikyam vs Kasimali S/O Hussainpeera on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121167142/
5  attendant charges, food,
nourishment, conveyance, etc.,.
5. Towards loss of future income 2,24,640 due to disability.

Less: Compensation awarded by 1,75,884  tribunal:
 Enhanced compensation: 1,68,590 11.
Therefore, the claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,44,474/- as against Rs.1,75,884/- awarded by the tribunal.

The claimant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.1,68,590/- (Rs.3,44,474/- minus Rs.1,75,884/-), along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

12. The insurance company is at liberty to file execution case before the jurisdictional executing Court directly for recovery of the amount from the owner of lorry and also may seek an order of attachment of movables and immovable properties or both till the amount is recovered.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) MFA No.101756/2019 filed by the claimant is allowed in part.
ii) MFA No.100951/2019 filed by the insurance company is allowed in part.

iii) The judgment and award dated 29.12.2018 passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gangavathi, in M.V.C. No.322/2016,
stands modified.
